acceptance: A cycle that FAILs from a phase-level/infra error (launch refusal, timeout, abort) records that error into state FailReasons — 'FinalVerdict: FAIL' with FailReasons null/empty becomes structurally impossible (bytestability/regression test).

The recorded reason carries the failure-adapter class and the originating phase (e.g. 'phase router: bridge launch refused: fleet mode: explicit worktree required'), so retros and the identical-fingerprint breaker get real identities instead of content-free fingerprints (the bc2e3236 lesson, task-FAIL variant).

The known mechanism from instance 1 is fixed or itemized: advisor/router REPLAN dispatch under fleet mode launched without a designated worktree and was correctly refused (cycle-1358 router-launch-error.txt) — either designate the worktree on the replan path or fall back to a sanctioned scratch cwd for the router agent.

fix: Two halves: (1) outcome sealing — when a cycle fails from a phase error rather than an audit verdict, write the phase error (class + phase + message head) into FailReasons before sealing, so no FAIL is reason-less; (2) the one diagnosed mechanism — the router replan dispatch must designate a worktree (or sanctioned scratch) under fleet mode instead of being refused.
problem: Cycles can seal 'FinalVerdict: FAIL' with FailReasons null when the failure happens at phase-infra level (launch refusal/abort) instead of audit. Three instances in one night. Cost: retros fingerprint nothing (content-free identity — the exact defect class bc2e3236 fixed for gate-blocks), the breaker cannot see genuine recurrence, and infra failures hide behind task-shaped FAILs.
